newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Old Mutual sees gilts down to 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Old Mutual sees gilts down to 13 pct.

text.p: South Africa's Old Mutual investment institution sees South Africa bond yields sliding to around 13 percent over the next year as the central Reserve Bank eases up on monetary policy.
"We could see long gilts moving down further from the existing 14.3 percent level, reflecting growing expectations of cuts in prime," gilt fund portfolio manager Mark le Roux said on Monday.

"While the prospect of a prime rate cut is already discounted to some extent in existing gilt prices, rates could still fall sharply as the downswing in South African interest rates gets under way," he said.
Analysts told Reuters last week they expected Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals to cut the South African central bank's key interest rate from 17 percent to 16 percent between August and October.
Analysts said they expected three or four cuts in the downward cycle, which is likely to continue throughout 1998.
A Reuter survey of 24 economists in June showed that most expected the bank rate to drop two percentage points by the end of the first quarter of 1998.
"Barring an unforeseen currency shock, once the first cut has taken place, a second and third seems likely in 1998 and a prolonged downswing in rates should be under way," le Roux said.
"This augurs well for gilts," he said.
